chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nadhr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Names of Allah and their derivation: From what is 'Allah' derived?

He said: So he said to me: O Hisham, 'Allah' is derived from 'ilah' (god/deity), and 'al-ilah' connotes the one who is worshipped (ma'luh). The name is other than the named. Whoever worships the name without the meaning, he has disbelieved and has not worshipped anything. Whoever worships the name and the meaning, he has disbelieved and worshipped two. Whoever worships the meaning without the name, that is Tawhid (divine unity). Have you understood, O Hisham?

He said: I said: Increase for me. He said: Indeed, Allah has ninety-nine names. If the name were identical to the named, then every one of these names would be a god. But Allah is a meaning to which these names allude, and each of them is other than Him. O Hisham, 'bread' is a name for what is eaten, 'water' is a name for what is drunk, 'clothes' is a name for what is worn, 'fire' is a name for what burns. Have you understood, O Hisham, with an understanding by which you can repel and contend with our enemies and those who take other than Allah as a deity?
I said: Yes. He said: May Allah benefit you by it and make you firm, O Hisham. Hisham said: By Allah, no one has defeated me in Tawhid until I stood in this position.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between worshipping the name of God and worshipping His meaning in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Shia theological distinction between the divine essence and its linguistic appellations, a key concept in understanding *Tawhid* (monotheism). Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while 'Allah' is derived from 'ilah', the name is merely a pointer to the transcendent meaning, preventing the error of idolizing the word itself. This nuanced view safeguards against both literalism and polytheism, affirming that true worship is directed solely at the divine reality behind the names.

en.ammaar-muslim: 2. [2/388] al-Kafi: Ali b. Ibrahim from his father from al-Nadhr b. Suwayd from Hisham b. al-Hakam - that he asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about the Names of Allah and their derivation saying: What is Allah derived from?

He (Hisham) said: So he (the Imam) said to me: O Hisham, ‘Allah’ is derived from ‘ilah’ and ‘al-ilah’ connotes the one who is worshipped. The name is other than the named. Whoever worships the name without the meaning then he has disbelieved and has not worshipped anything. Whoever worships the name and the meaning then he has disbelieved and worshipped two (distinct things). Whoever worships the meaning without the name then that is Tawhid. Have you understood O Hisham?

He (Hisham) said: I said: increase for me. He said: Allah has ninety nine names, if the name was identical to what is named then every name among these (ninety-nine) would be a god, rather Allah is a meaning to which these names allude to, and each one of them is other than him. O Hisham, ‘bread’ is a name for what is eaten, ‘water’ is a name for what is drunk, ‘clothes’ is a name for what is worn, ‘fire’ is a name for what burns. Have you understood Hisham? an understanding through which you can repel and defeat our enemies and those who betake others apart from Allah Mighty and Majestic (alone).
I said: Yes. He said: May Allah benefit you by it and make you firm O Hisham.Hisham said: By Allah no one has defeated me on the subject of Tawhid to this day when I stand in the position I do.
